req.title: Create schema on startup
req.statement: The system shall create the tasks table via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-024 requires that the tasks table is created via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup. The primary observable effect is that the app is reachable (HTTP 200 on root) and the /tasks/ endpoint returns HTTP 200 with the pre-loaded rows, proving the table exists. Positive: app starts and root returns exact payload. Negative: querying a non-existent task returns 404 (table exists but row absent). Boundary: the tasks table has exactly 20 pre-loaded rows; querying with default limit returns all 20, and querying id=20 (last valid) vs id=21 (first invalid) exercises the boundary of the seeded dataset and confirms the schema is fully operational.

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_root_endpoint_returns_exact_welcome_payload():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body["message"] == "Welcome to Task Manager API"
    assert body["docs"] == "/docs"
    assert body["version"] == "1.0.0"
    assert len(body) == 3

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_tasks_table_exists_and_returns_preloaded_rows():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/tasks/")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    tasks = r.json()
    assert isinstance(tasks, list)
    assert len(tasks) == 20
    first = tasks[0]
    assert first["id"] == 1
    assert first["title"] == "Read chapter 5"
    assert first["completed"] == True
    last = tasks[19]
    assert last["id"] == 20
    assert last["title"] == "Reply to emails"
    assert last["completed"] == False

tests.name: test_startup_schema_allows_task_creation_and_retrieval
expected: Response contains id, title, description, completed, created_at
GET returns HTTP 200 with same task data
trace: R-TASK-024: schema creation enables write and read operations
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_schema_allows_task_creation_and_retrieval():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {"title": "Startup test task", "description": "Created in test", "completed": False}
    r = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    created = r.json()
    assert created["title"] == "Startup test task"
    assert created["description"] == "Created in test"
    assert created["completed"] == False
    assert "id" in created
    assert "created_at" in created
    task_id = created["id"]
    r2 = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    fetched = r2.json()
    assert fetched["id"] == task_id
    assert fetched["title"] == "Startup test task"

test_startup_schema_allows_task_creation_and_retrieval()

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_completed_filter_true_returns_only_completed_tasks():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/tasks/?completed=true")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    tasks = r.json()
    assert isinstance(tasks, list)
    assert len(tasks) == 6
    for t in tasks:
        assert t["completed"] == True
    ids = {t["id"] for t in tasks}
